definitions.explanation: A substance that gives color to something, whether natural (such as melanin in skin) or artificial (such as food coloring).

examples.japanese: {紫外線|しがいせん}を{浴|あ}びると{色素|しきそ}が{沈着|ちんちゃく}する。
examples.english: Exposure to UV rays causes pigmentation.

examples.japanese: この{食品|しょくひん}には{人工|じんこう}{色素|しきそ}が{使|つか}われていないので{安心|あんしん}だ。
examples.english: This food product doesn't use artificial coloring, so it's safe.

notes:
A compound of {色|しき} (color) and {素|そ} (element, substance). Used broadly in biology, medicine, food science, and cosmetics to refer to any substance responsible for color.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {色素|しきそ}{沈着|ちんちゃく} — pigmentation (deposit of pigment in skin)
- {人工|じんこう}{色素|しきそ} — artificial coloring
- {天然|てんねん}{色素|しきそ} — natural pigment
- {色素|しきそ}が{薄|うす}い — to have light pigmentation
- メラニン{色素|しきそ} — melanin pigment

RELATED TERMS:
- {着色料|ちゃくしょくりょう} — coloring agent (for food/products)
- {染料|せんりょう} — dye (for fabrics)
- {顔料|がんりょう} — pigment (for paints and inks)
